newsitem.title: USA: U.S. corporate bonds unchanged in light trade.
newsitem.headline: U.S. corporate bonds unchanged in light trade.

text.p: U.S. high-grade corporate bonds were unchanged in light volume as players returned from their extended holiday, dealers said.
On Monday, the U.S. Treasury and fixed-income markets were closed in observance of the Columbus Day holiday.
"It was a quiet opening," said one high-grade trader. "Volume is light and spreads are unchanged on the day."
Some interest was seen on the retail side, but traders said the street was relatively quiet.
Meanwhile, news that Conrail Inc and CSX Corp would merge in an $8.4 billion deal left spreads on the companies' debt unchanged, traders said.
"Spreads on Conrail and CSX Corp were unmoved by the news," one industrials trader said.
Traders said activity was also affected by the absence of new corporate debt issues on Tuesday after a week that featured about $6.0 billion in new straight debt.
But given the market's positive rate environment and strong investor interest, corporate debt issuance is expected to heat up once again, traders said.
"Levels are still very good so the trend toward strong issuance should continue," one syndicate source said.
Meanwhile, Citicorp is expected to tap the market with $200 million in A2/A rated 15-year subordinated notes on Tuesday via Bear Stearns & Co, market sources said.
The notes are expected to price between 75 and 77 basis points over the 10-year U.S. Treasury note, sources added.
Goodyear is also expected to issue $100 million in debt via Morgan Stanley, sources said.
Another $300 million in yankee debt is expected to price out of British Sky Broadcasting, dealers said.
In the corporate high-yield sector prices were mostly unchanged, but Harrah's Jazz bonds were seen trading higher, traders said.
"It's been a quiet day overall in the secondary market but Harrah's Jazz bonds were the exception...they're up a point," one high-yield trader said.
The bonds were quoted up one point at 58 bid.
Marvel Entertainment debt was quoted unchanged at 48 bid despite the company's announcement that it would report net losses for the third quarter and that as a result it had violated its bank loans.
Traders said the company's debt had been experiencing downward pressure for some time, trading in lockstep with the company's stock.
"These (Marvel) bonds were trading at 58 bid at one point, then traded down to 54 and then to 52. Today the market is unchanged at 48 bid," one high-yield trader said.
Last week, Moody's Investors Service cut Marvel Entertainment debt ratings following the news.
--Nancy Leinfuss, 212-859-1675
